jordan (eng-ml): noticing a weird regression when bringing up a new HF chat_template -> Redwood prompt conversion for the 4-bit quantized build. evals drop ~6% QA F1 after conversion :eyes:

sophia (eng-ml): can you paste the jinja + config and the converted prompt?

jordan (eng-ml): small repro below. original HF template:

```jinja
{% if system %}- role: system
  content: "{{ system }}"
{% endif %}
- role: user
  content: |
    {% if include_intro %}{{ intro }}
    ---
    {% endif %}{{ question }}
```

and config.json has: "special_tokens_map": {"bos_token": "<s>", "eos_token": "</s>", "pad_token": "<pad>", "additional_special_tokens": ["<|assistant|>", "<|user|>", "<|system|>"] }

converted Redwood prompt we used (rough):

```
System: {{ system }}

User: {{ intro }}
---
{{ question }}
Assistant:
```

liam (eng-runtime): what's the exact quantized model? 4-bit GPT-like? which tokenizer?

jordan (eng-ml): 4bit-llama-compat, huggingface tokenizer with added extra tokens above. tokenizer.encode shows occasional split of "<|assistant|>" into "<|ass" and "istant|>" on certain byte boundaries after quantization tokenization normalization. seems to change token boundaries when we do the final prompt flattening.

sophia (eng-ml): that token split could cause the runtime to mis-detect role markers, so redwood conversion maybe relies on whole-token sentinels. if sentinel breaks, assistant role prefix gets swallowed -> model sees as a continuation of user -> hallucinations/regression.

marcus (eng-ml): saw something like this before: whitespace control in Jinja combined with `|` chars and our prompt sanitizer collapsed the sentinel into surrounding text. can you show what the actual rendered bytes look like?

jordan (eng-ml): here's an example of rendered prompt bytes (hex) and token ids: `... 3c 7c 61 73 73 69 73 74 61 6e 7c 3e ...` but in the quantized tokenizer pipeline we hit a normalization step that turns `\nUser:` into `\n User:` (extra space) for certain unicode normalizations, pushing the sentinel over the boundary.

tanya (eng-infra): can we reproduce in a tiny script? if deterministic we can add to onboarding tests.

jordan (eng-ml): repro gist: <https://gist.github.com/rw/repro-jinja-sentinel-split> (private) - steps:
1) load HF tokenizer with additional_special_tokens
2) render template with and without jinja whitespace control (`-` strips)
3) compare tokenization of sentinel sequences
4) run convert_to_redwood_prompt() (our converter) then tokenization again

sophia (eng-ml): quick hypothesis: our converter strips consecutive blank lines and trims leading/trailing spaces on each role block. when the sentinel sits at the left edge, trimming can remove the leading `<` or replace it with an ASCII space when the newline is normalized. two fixes: (A) make converter escape/preserve special tokens by wrapping them in zero-width joiner markers before trimming, or (B) enforce sentinel mapping using tokenizer.special_tokens_map during conversion (i.e., insert token ids rather than raw strings).

liam (eng-runtime): (B) seems safer long-term. if we convert sentinel to token ids before any string-level whitespace ops we won't rely on fragile string boundaries. downside: complicates eval diffs because stored prompts are no longer plain text.

marcus (eng-ml): temporary patch idea: in converter, run a regex that reconstitutes broken token pieces: `re.sub(r"<\|ass\s+istant\|>", "<|assistant|>", s)` — ugly but fast. we should still add a unit test.

qa-bot: NEW ISSUE created: RW-2468 - "jinja whitespace + special token splitting causes role sentinel split on quantized tokenizers" (labels: p1, eng-ml)

jordan (eng-ml): repro eval numbers: baseline FP16 -> QA F1 78.2, converted+FP16 -> 78.0, converted+4bit -> 71.5. converting without touching sentinels -> 77.8 on 4bit. so conversion step causes ~6.3 absolute drop on quantized run.

sophia (eng-ml): thanks. assign to eng-ml pair to triage. short-term action items:
- add targeted unit test in onboarding harness that tokenizes rendered prompt before/after conversion and asserts sentinel tokens remain intact (marcus)
- try conversion-by-ids fallback in runtime for quantized models (liam)
- add Jinja whitespace examples to our conversion docs (jordan)

tanya (eng-infra): will add a CI job that tokenizes with the same quantized tokenizer in the model bring-up pipeline so we catch this earlier.

liam (eng-runtime): I'll prototype conversion-by-ids. if we do that, we should also log a checksum of sentinel token ids in console so we can detect silent splits in future rollouts.

marcus (eng-ml): patched a minimal unit test and a regex hotfix in my branch, pushing PR now: `# PR 5371`

jordan (eng-ml): awesome. leaving the repro gist and eval logs in the ticket. @sophia can you add a note to the onboarding checklist to explicitly run `tokenizer.convert_tokens_to_ids(additional_special_tokens)` and assert presence?

sophia (eng-ml): yup, adding it now. :thumbsup:

liam (eng-runtime): once PR lands let's run the quantized eval suite again.

jordan (eng-ml): thanks all, will monitor RW-2468 and post back if anything else pops up. :sparkles:
